McLaren: McLaren has fitted a bigger engine cover to boost cooling, a sturdier front suspension for Monaco’s bumpy streets, and a tweaked rear‑wing cascade to trim drag on this circuit. They’ve also refined the beam wing, rear corner and diffuser to smooth airflow and keep the car stable through fast corners. All of these tweaks mean the car should stay cooler, feel more planted and be quicker on the straights—exactly what the team needs to be competitive this weekend.
Mercedes F1 Team: Mercedes has slipped a few tiny winglets into the rear‑wing fairing. The extra surfaces give the car a bit more rear‑end grip, helping it stay stable through fast corners and under heavy braking. That extra stability could translate into better tyre wear and more confidence for the drivers over this weekend’s high‑speed layout.
Racing Bulls / RB: Racing Bulls has beefed up the front‑wheel area and the engine‑cover exits, so the car stays cooler and less prone to overheating – a crucial reliability boost for a weekend where high‑speed laps can push temperatures to the limit. The rear wing now features a longer third element, an extra flap and a new winglet, giving the car a stronger rear push and more stable handling through the fast corners. Together, these tweaks aim to keep the car on the track longer and extract extra grip when it matters most.
Scuderia Ferrari: Ferrari has reshaped the front‑end of the car for this circuit, tweaking the suspension arms and the fairings that sit around them to give the car a more stable, predictable feel through the twisty sections. They’ve also added a small “gurney” flap on the front part of the floor and a new support strut on the back of the diffuser, both aimed at fine‑tuning the balance between downforce and drag so the car can corner harder without sacrificing straight‑line speed. In short, these tweaks should make the SF‑something more planted on the bends and quicker on the straights, giving the drivers a better platform to attack the weekend’s challenges.
Williams Racing: Williams has tweaked the front‑end of the car, changing the suspension geometry and the surface of the surrounding panels to give the tyres better contact and more stable handling. They’ve also re‑routed the exhaust tailpipe, which improves the way exhaust gases flow and helps the engine stay in its optimal power band. Together, these changes should make the car feel more predictable in corners and give a small boost in straight‑line performance for the upcoming weekend.
Aston Martin: Aston Martin has tweaked the front suspension geometry, added a few extra cooling vents and reshaped the rear‑exhaust bracket. The suspension tweak sharpens turn‑in and stability, the extra louvers keep the engine and brakes from overheating on a hot circuit, and the exhaust change improves rear‑end balance. Together they give the car more grip, better reliability and a stronger push off the line for this weekend’s race.
Haas F1 Team: Haas has refined the front‑suspension geometry to give the car a sharper turn‑in and more stability through the high‑speed corners this weekend. At the back, engineers have re‑balanced the rear wing’s load and stiffened the rear impact structure, which should tighten the car’s rear‑end grip and keep the car more predictable under braking. Together, these changes aim to boost overall handling and confidence, letting the drivers push harder on the circuit.
Audi F1 Team: Audi has stripped the movable flaps (SM actuators) from both the front and rear wings, a circuit‑specific change that simplifies the aero set‑up and cuts the chance of a wing‑related failure on the bumpy track. The side mirrors have been reshaped to clean up airflow and give the driver clearer sightlines, while the roll‑hoop and engine cover have been re‑designed to improve cooling and reduce drag. All three tweaks should make the car more stable and quicker over this weekend’s demanding circuit.
Alpine F1 Team: Alpine has bolted a few small winglets onto the rear wing, giving the car a bite of extra down‑force right where it’s needed most. The tweak should tighten up the car’s rear end in the high‑speed corners, helping drivers carry more speed and keep the tyres in the sweet spot. In short, it’s a modest aerodynamic boost that could translate into a few tenths of a second around the circuit this weekend.
Cadillac: Cadillac has tweaked the shape of its rear wing and the end‑plates, giving the car a more aggressive “scoop” that sticks it to the tarmac a bit harder, especially through fast corners. At the same time, the exhaust pipe and its mounting brackets have been reshaped to smooth out the flow of hot gases, sharpening throttle response and giving a quick‑kick of power on the straights. Together, these tweaks should make the Cadillac more stable in the bends and faster out of the exits, turning the weekend into a real chance for a podium push.
